newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian inquiry boss orders share disposal.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian inquiry boss orders share disposal.

text.p: Stan Wallis, the chief of an inquiry into Australia's financial system, said on Sunday he had required members of the inquiry committee to sell all shares they owned in any Australian financial group.
Wallis, recently appointed president of the Business Council of Australia, said in a television interview that he had divested his shares and had made sure members of his committee did the same.
"I do not own a bank share or shares in a financial institution and it has been a very expensive decision," he said on the Business Sunday programme.
Asked about the rest of the committee, Wallis said: "We have made sure we are all in good shape."
Last month Australia's federal government was bruised by allegations that a number of government members of parliament held shares in companies where there could be a perceived conflict of interest.
It was unclear if Wallis' share disposal requirement was in response to those allegations.
Australia's conservative coalition promised the finance sector inquiry in the run-up to the federal election which it won in a landside in March this year.

The major issue is to decide whether mergers should be allowed between the big four banks, National Australia Bank Ltd, Westpac Banking Corp, Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd and the Commonwealth Bank of Australia Ltd.
The inquiry is due to conclude by March next year with a draft report ready this month.
Breaches of Prime Minister John Howard's ministerial guidelines on share ownership led to the resignation of two junior government members last month.
Under the ministerial guidelines, government members are required to divest any investments which may conflict with their portfolio.
